root_idea.summary: The root centers on binding or holding fast, extending to physical restraints, fastening devices, binding obligations, and ties that incline one toward another.
root_idea.development: The semantic range develops from physical confinement and fastening to covenants, burdensome obligations, kinship bonds, barriers, and forms of neighboring through shared tent fastenings.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized noun citation form إِصْرٌ.

senses.definition: A binding covenant, compact, or solemn obligation.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage, it denotes an affirmed covenant or obligation whose binding force bears on the one who undertakes or breaks it.

senses.definition: A burdensome obligation, restriction, or load that holds a person back.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of obligations or burdens that restrain people from ease, good works, or attainment of reward, including burdens associated with earlier communities.

senses.definition: A sin or offense; in one interpretation, the grievous punishment associated with sin.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an explicitly reported Quranic interpretation of إِصْرٌ in 2:286, especially in connection with the offense of breaking a covenant or its resulting punishment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To confine, restrict, detain, withhold, hinder, or prevent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may take a person or thing as object; أَصَرَهُ عَلَى denotes restricting someone to an affair, while أَصَرَهُ عَنْ denotes withholding or debarring him from a desired thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fasten a tent with an إِصَارٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized construction referring to putting the tent’s lower fastening rope or peg in place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break something.
To bend or incline something, or to cause someone to incline toward another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction can describe physical bending or an inclination toward a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be a neighbor, with one tent’s fastening beside another’s.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense describes neighboring through adjacent tent fastenings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be neighbors or dwell near one another.
A bond or tie that inclines one toward another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The tie may arise from a relationship, covenant, compact, contract, or similar bond; this classical relational use is distinct from the Quranic covenantal and burdensome uses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An oath carrying an inescapable obligation to divorce, emancipate, or fulfill a vow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized expression for an exceptionally binding oath for which no ordinary expiation is available.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hole of the ear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct anatomical usage, with a plural form reported as آصَارٌ or إِصْرَانٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A short rope, peg, or thong used to fasten or bind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially the rope or peg securing the lower part of a tent; it may also denote a thong of untanned hide binding parts of a camel’s saddle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cloth containing and tied around dry herbage or fodder; also the gathered dry fodder itself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Some descriptions restrict the term to fodder enclosed in a cloth or otherwise collected together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A basket in which goods or commodities are carried.
Pasturage so abundant that it detains those who are upon it or draws people toward it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective describes abundance as causing people to remain at or go to the pasture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tether or tie to which a beast is fastened.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A term for the fastening point or tie used to secure an animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tie of kinship, affinity, favor, or benefit that inclines one toward someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can denote the relationship or favor itself; a poetic interpretation also understands female relatives metonymically as such ties.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cloth bundle tied with dry grass or fodder and folded over a camel’s hump to facilitate riding.
A place in which a person or thing is confined, shut up, or imprisoned.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Variant vocalization مَأْصَرٌ is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A barrier between two things that prevents passage; specifically, a rope stretched across a road or waterway to stop travelers or boats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The road or waterway barrier is described in connection with collecting tithes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A neighbor, especially one living close by.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression evokes adjoining tent fastenings as the basis of the neighborhood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tribe or group dwelling or abiding near together.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Core Form I confinement and restraint sense.
Personal inclination is covered by the broader inclination sense.
Form III neighboring through adjacent tent fastenings.
Form VI neighboring and dwelling near.
Covenant, burden, relational bond, and binding-oath branches.
Weight or burden branch covered by the Quranic burden sense.
Quran-attested sin, offense, and punishment interpretation.
Thing that inclines one toward another.
Fastening implement sense with a poetic relational interpretation.
Fodder enclosed in a tied cloth.
Pasture whose abundance detains or attracts.
Kinship, affinity, favor, or benefit as an inclining tie.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence at 2:286 carries variant lexical interpretations in the evidence: a burdensome obligation, a sin or offense, and a grievous punishment; the contextual rendering supplied is “a burden.”
